lens: Recompute every printed number from its producing artifact; check every count against the actual length of the list it counts, every statistic against the gene set it is attributed to, and every denominator against the samples actually used.
central_claim: Five therapeutic classes that are prescribed on a molecular state rather than a histology were checked against the public EMC expression record; for four the selecting state is absent, each negative is graded separately for strength, and only the BH3-mimetic class stays open.

blockers.summary: Section 1 prints 'Two public series - the only readable EMC expression data that exists.' A THIRD public EMC expression series exists (GSE28866, 4 EMC samples), and the paper's own source artifact records it, records that its 'unreadable' grade is a property of the file format rather than of the data, and states in terms that the grade 'must never be quoted' as a finding that no usable data exists. The paper quotes it as exactly that. This converts an absent reading into a reading of absence - the standing rule the paper itself invokes two paragraphs later - and it moves the paper's headline denominator, which is 16 EMC tumours.
blockers.evidence: emc-expression-panels.json -> reads.read_8_SURFACE_ANTIGEN.CSPG4_platform_discordance.what_would_actually_decide_it[0]. Key 'decider': 'A THIRD, INDEPENDENT EMC SERIES. This is the direct tie-breaker, and it is NOT hypothetical.' Key '(star)_a_third_series_exists_and_the_reason_it_is_unread_is_measured': 'GSE28866 carries 4 EMC samples against 27 normal/reference samples ... It is graded unreadable, and the DIAGNOSTIC for that grade ... is in the inputs cache: its series matrix reports n_probes: 0 across 99 samples on GPL10999 ... the processed data lives in the series SUPPLEMENTARY files, which this instrument never looks at.' Key '(stop)_so_the_grade_is_about_the_file_format_not_the_data': "'Unreadable' here means THIS READER could not parse THAT file. It is not a finding that GSE28866 holds no usable expression data, and it must never be quoted as one (CLAUDE.md section 4)." The same block records that a processed matrix DOES exist in GEO ('GSE28866_36048_normalized_peaks_cancer_and_normal.txt.gz') and names the four EMC samples (GSM715466 STT5525_EMC, GSM715467 STT5526_EMC, GSM715470 STT5527_EMC, GSM715472 STT5592_EMC). Independently corroborated in code: emc_cohort_search.py line 89 records GSE28866 as '3SEQ arm (4 EMC); the Brunner et al. lncRNA deposit' and line 116 lists it among POSITIVE_CONTROLS alongside GSE24369 and GSE4303; aso_delivery_antigen.py line 625 uses it as 'GSE28866 / 3SEQ - 4 EMC vs 32 non-EMC sarcoma libraries, read density', i.e. another module in this repository has already read expression from it.
blockers.what_edit_would_break_it: Replace 'the only readable EMC expression data that exists' with a statement about what THIS instrument could parse, and say what was left unread and why - e.g. 'the two series this array-based reader can parse; a third public EMC series (GSE28866, 4 EMC samples) is a sequencing deposit whose processed matrix sits in GEO supplementary files this reader does not open, so it is unread here rather than absent.' Adding that sentence also makes the 16-tumour denominator honest. Any phrasing that keeps an existence claim about the world, rather than a scope claim about the reader, leaves the blocker standing.

p1s.summary: Section 2.3 attributes t = -0.22 and 1.71 to 'the rest of PRC2', but those two numbers are the score of the FULL prc2_core group, which INCLUDES EZH2 - the gene the same sentence has just separated out. Recomputing with EZH2 removed gives t = -1.41 (GPL6244) and t = 0.448 (GPL3290). The GPL3290 figure is wrong by a factor of ~3.8 for the set it is attributed to, and it is wrong in the direction that matters: EZH2 is the single gene carrying that platform's PRC2 signal.
p1s.evidence: Paper section 2.3: 'EZH2 is mildly higher on both platforms and the rest of PRC2 is flat (*t* = -0.22 and 1.71)'. emc-expression-panels.json -> panels.chromatin_prc2_baf.groups.prc2_core.genes_requested = ['EZH2','EED','SUZ12','RBBP4']; score.t = -0.216 (GSE24369) and 1.714 (GSE4303-GPL3290). I reimplemented the group statistic (per-sample mean of z_vs_array over readable members, then Welch on EMC vs comparator) from gene_reads.*.per_sample and reproduced EVERY published group t in the paper to 3 dp exactly - prc2 -0.216/1.714, swi_snf -1.024/-0.083, guardians -4.568/-2.538, alt-EJ 2.423/2.226, HR -0.573/1.035, NHEJ -0.192/0.158, p53 output -2.203/-1.126 - together with the published df and group means, which validates the method. Dropping EZH2 from that same computation yields t = -1.410 (EED,SUZ12,RBBP4; GPL6244) and t = 0.448 (EED,RBBP4; GPL3290, SUZ12 unreadable there). EZH2 alone on GPL3290 is delta +0.6291 SD, t = 2.839. Provenance note: the grading artifact's own sentence (census-route-expression-grading.json -> routes['RT-EZH2'].observed) is 'EZH2 is mildly higher on both platforms and the rest of PRC2 is flat' with NO t-values; the manuscript added the parenthetical, so the misattribution originates in the prose.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Either name the set correctly ('the PRC2 core as a whole is flat, t = -0.22 and 1.71') or quote the EZH2-excluded figures and regenerate them into emc-expression-panels.json so they have a home. The qualitative conclusion survives either way and is in fact better supported by 0.45 than by 1.71.

p1s.summary: The paper prints 'three of the five' twice as the count of classes whose deciding measurement is not a transcript. Counted against the paper's own falsifier table and its own section text, the number is five. No reading of the document yields three.
p1s.evidence: Section 3: 'For three of the five the deciding measurement is a protein, a mutation or a functional assay, and each is named in its own section.' Section 5: 'A transcript is not a protein, a mutation or a dependency, and for three of the five classes the selecting feature is one of those three rather than a transcript level.' Enumerating the deciding measurement each section actually names: 2.1 arginine - 'ASS1 loss in the source literature is an immunohistochemistry call, and a transcript is not a protein' (protein), falsifier F1 'ASS1 immunohistochemistry'; 2.2 MDM2 - 'This cannot establish that TP53 is wild-type or mutant', F2 'a TP53 sequence call plus a stress-response readout' (mutation); 2.3 EZH2 - 'The approved indication is selected by protein loss', F3 'INI1/SMARCB1 immunohistochemistry' (protein); 2.4 Pol-theta - 'An HR defect is usually a mutation', F4 'a mutational or genomic-scar readout' (mutation); 2.5 BH3 - 'the method that measures it is BH3 profiling', F7 'BH3 profiling on EMC tissue or a model - the decisive test' (functional assay / dependency). That is 5/5 under section 3's triple (protein, mutation, functional assay) and 5/5 under section 5's triple (protein, mutation, dependency). Excluding 2.1 to reach three is directly contradicted by 2.1's own sentence; excluding 2.2 is contradicted by F2.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Change both instances to 'five' (or to 'every one of the five'), or state explicitly which three are meant and why the other two are excluded. Section 3's trailing clause 'and each is named in its own section' is the internal check that fails: all five sections name one.

p1s.summary: Five solitary fibrous tumours from GSE24369 - same series, same platform, bona fide soft-tissue sarcomas - are dropped from the comparator arm by a gap in a string-matching classifier, not by a stated rule, and the paper discloses no exclusion. The paper's table reports '29 comparator sarcomas'; the series carries 34 non-EMC tumour samples. Every GPL6244 contrast in sections 2.2-2.5 is computed against the reduced arm.
p1s.evidence: emc-expression-panels.json -> platforms['GSE24369_series_matrix.txt.gz']: n_samples = 42, n_EMC = 6, n_comparator = 29, so 7 samples are unused. From sample_annotations_verbatim the class tally is desmoid_fibromatosis 6, EMC 6, LGFMS 17, fibrosarcoma 6, unclassified 7; the seven unused GSMs are GSM600963-967 ('Solitary fibrous tumor 1-5 | soft tissue | sample type: tumor biopsy') and GSM600968-969 ('Skeletal muscle pooled RNA 1-2'). The two pooled-normal samples are correctly out. The five solitary fibrous tumours are out because emc_atr_vulnerability.py COMPARATOR_BUCKETS (lines 294-323) contains no 'solitary fibrous' pattern, so _classify_sample falls through to 'unclassified' (line 1619), and emc_expression_panels.py _group_indices (lines 1647-1654) excludes 'unclassified' from BOTH arms. Non-EMC tumour samples in the series = 6+17+6+5 = 34, against the 29 the paper prints. I could not quantify the effect: gene_reads[*][GSE24369].per_sample contains only the 35 used samples (verified: len = 35, GSM600963 absent), and the series matrix is not in the repository, so re-including them needs a GEO fetch. The paper contains no occurrence of 'solitary', 'exclud(ed)', 'dropped' or 'unclassified' in a methods sense (grep of the manuscript).
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: State the exclusion in section 1 - how many samples the series holds, how many entered each arm, and that five solitary fibrous tumours were dropped as unclassified - or add 'solitary fibrous' to COMPARATOR_BUCKETS, regenerate, and re-quote every GPL6244 t. Disclosure alone removes the defect; silence is what makes it one.

p2s.summary: Section 2.3's 'no SWI/SNF tumour-suppressor subunit reads anywhere near a floor' is evidenced by t = -1.02 and -0.08, but those are EMC-versus-comparator CONTRAST statistics. A contrast near zero says EMC resembles its comparators; it says nothing about absolute level, which is what 'near a floor' asserts. The statistic that does address it - the array percentile - is not quoted, and one subunit sits low on one platform.
p2s.evidence: emc-expression-panels.json gene_reads EMC mean_array_percentile on GSE4303-GPL3290: SMARCB1 0.5187, SMARCA4 0.5341, PBRM1 0.3579, ARID1A 0.1825 (on GPL6244: 0.7744, 0.818, 0.5512, 0.8344). ARID1A reads in the bottom fifth of its array on GPL3290. The artifact's own _limits entry warns that 'An array_percentile on GPL3290 is a percentile of log-RATIOS, which is not the same statement as expressed', which is a further reason the floor claim cannot rest on either statistic. The registrational biomarker, SMARCB1, is at the 77th and 52nd percentile, so the substantive conclusion holds - it is the evidence cited for it that does not measure it.

p2s.summary: 'In a disease with perhaps a few hundred patients diagnosed per year worldwide' has no home in any committed artifact and sits in tension with the repository's own registry figure, which the paper does not reconcile or cite.
p2s.evidence: grep for 'few hundred patients' across research/ and systems/ returns this manuscript plus emc-unexplored-treatment-lanes.md and three systems views, all of which use the phrase for reconstructable COHORT sizes, not annual incidence. research/data/emc-clinical-registry.json line 22: 'Roughly 1-3% of all soft-tissue sarcomas. Estimated incidence is well under 1 per million per year.' Taken at face value against world population, 'well under 1 per million per year' bounds the figure in the low thousands rather than the low hundreds, and the registry's other statement (1-3% of soft-tissue sarcomas) points the same way. The manuscript's figure is hedged with 'perhaps', so this is not a false claim - but it is an unsourced number in the sentence that carries the paper's motivation.

p2s.summary: Section 1 attributes the H-EMC-SS fusion-status record to depmap-sarcoma-dependency.json, which contains no such record.
p2s.evidence: The sentence 'That panel contains no EMC line - the one line carrying the disease's label is recorded as not harbouring the fusion' follows immediately on the link to research/modalities/depmap-sarcoma-dependency.json. grep of that file for 'H-EMC', 'hemcss' or 'label' returns 0 hits; it holds only genes_by_group, context_genes, nr4a_paralogue_comparison, self_validation, BRD9_by_fusion_sarcoma_subtype and fusion_addiction_proxy. The record actually lives in research/modalities/hemcss-label-priorart.json, whose own _status field reads 'INCOMPLETE. Stopped 2026-08-15 ... This is a PARTIAL record with honest boundaries, NOT a survey.' Cite that file (and its status) rather than letting the DepMap link carry the claim.

p2s.summary: 'MCL1 and BCL2L1 are dependencies in the large majority of sarcoma lines' is accurate (0.835 and 0.758), but the following sentence upgrades it to 'a near-universal dependency', which 76-84% does not support; and the denominator behind those fractions is 91 screened lines, while the same artifact's headline field reports 176 sarcoma models.
p2s.evidence: depmap-sarcoma-dependency.json genes_by_group['Apoptotic guardians (BH3)']: MCL1 sarcoma_frac_dependent 0.835, BCL2L1 0.758, both with n_sarcoma 91; top-level n_sarcoma_models 176. depmap_sarcoma_dependency.py lines 227-229 and 358 show 176 is the count of Soft Tissue/Bone models in Model.csv while 91 is the subset with CRISPR gene-effect data (line 259, n_sarcoma = len(s) after dropna), so both numbers are correct but only 91 is the denominator of the quoted fractions. The paper prints neither; the wording is the issue.

p2s.summary: Two selective quotations that a reader cannot resolve from the paper alone. Neither is an error.
p2s.evidence: (1) Section 2.1 quotes ASS1 at 'the 92nd percentile' on GPL6244 (emc_array_percentile 0.9152, verbatim from census-route-expression-grading.json routes['RT-ARGININE'].observed) but does not mention that on GPL3290 EMC ASS1 sits at the 41st percentile (0.4053) - the higher-than-comparator claim holds on both platforms (deltas +0.4787 and +1.5503), the high-absolute claim only on one. (2) Section 2.2 calls the p53 axis genes 'flat' on the strength of the group score (t = -0.601 and 0.432), which is correct, but MDM2 individually is the strongest single reading in that panel and is LOWER in EMC on both platforms (t = -3.337 and -1.922) - a result that corroborates the section's own 'quiet' conclusion and is omitted.

p2s.summary: Clean, and worth recording: none of this paper's ~20 printed statistics is registered in pinned-figures.json, so the repository's cross-copy consistency guard covers none of them.
p2s.evidence: research/manuscripts/pinned-figures.json: recursive search for 'biomarker-selected' returns no hit; targets is a 26-entry list with no entry for this document. The two literal string matches ('2.42', '1.74') belong to unrelated entries. This is an observation about guard coverage, not a defect in the manuscript.

_what_came_back_clean: Every group t-statistic printed in the paper reproduces EXACTLY from emc-expression-panels.json, recomputed independently from per-sample z-scores: p53 output -2.203/-1.126 (paper -2.20/-1.13), SWI/SNF -1.024/-0.083 (-1.02/-0.08), alt-EJ 2.423/2.226 (2.42/2.23), NHEJ -0.192/0.158 (-0.19/0.16), HR -0.573/1.035 (-0.57/1.04), guardians -4.568/-2.538 (-4.57/-2.54), p53 axis -0.601/0.432 ('flat'). Rounding is correct in every case.

16 EMC tumours = 6 (GSE24369) + 10 (GSE4303-GPL3290), matching platforms[*].n_EMC and the EMC_gsms lists (6 and 10 accessions). Section 1's table rows 6/29 and 10/6 match n_EMC and n_comparator exactly.
'NOXA ... HIGHER in EMC on both platforms, and on GPL3290 by 1.74 standard deviations': PMAIP1 delta_emc_minus_comparator = +0.2292 (GPL6244) and +1.7440 (GPL3290). Correct on both counts.
'MCL1 and BCL2L1 individually included' in the lower-guardian reading: MCL1 -0.2664/-0.5563, BCL2L1 -0.3801/-0.4755. Lower on both platforms, both genes.

'every readable member is higher on both' for alt-EJ: GPL6244 POLQ +0.0446, LIG3 +0.1148, PARP1 +0.0719, XRCC1 +0.1168; GPL3290 LIG3 +0.3386, PARP1 +0.2868, XRCC1 +0.1479 (POLQ unreadable there, correctly not counted). True as stated.
'EZH2 is mildly higher on both platforms': +0.0938 and +0.6291. True.
'ASS1 is HIGHER in EMC ... on both platforms': +0.4787 and +1.5503. True. The '92nd percentile' is 0.9152, correctly rounded and correctly attributed to GPL6244.
The internal arithmetic of the summary holds: five classes, four negatives, and the strength breakdown '1 clean + 2 proxy + 1 partial' sums to 4.
The falsifier table lists F1-F8 with no gap or duplicate, and every falsifier maps to a section.

All nine PMIDs printed in the manuscript (27735949, 28122247, 8440237, 33035459, 25642963, 25642960, 34179826, 17692808, 22230093) are present in biomarker-class-definitions-2026-08-09.json with titles, authors and DOIs. No identifier appears in the paper that is absent from the anchor file.
'MCL1 and BCL2L1 are dependencies in the large majority of sarcoma lines' is arithmetically correct against depmap-sarcoma-dependency.json (0.835, 0.758).
_verdict_note: Not 'not_supported_as_written', because the central claim is arithmetically sound: I recomputed all seven group statistics from the per-sample z-scores and reproduced the published t, df and group means to three decimal places, and every individual gene-level direction the paper asserts holds. Not 'supported', because one printed sentence ('the only readable EMC expression data that exists') is refuted by the paper's own source artifact, which names the third series and states in terms that its unreadable grade must never be quoted this way - and because a count printed twice ('three of the five') is contradicted by the paper's own falsifier table, and a statistic is attributed to a gene set that excludes the gene it was computed with. Recommendation is major_revision rather than minor because a blocker plus three P1s is more than a copy-edit; but every fix is textual - no reading changes, no artifact needs regenerating except optionally the PRC2 subset and the solitary-fibrous comparator arm.
